The lack of directly imaged cave reflectors beneath much of the temperate-ice zone suggests that temperate ice may reduce radar detectability of basal drainage features. These results provide geophysical evidence that LHG12 is not uniformly cold-based but contains a polythermal tongue with an organized subglacial drainage.
author: Tess Xianghuan Luo, Shuang Ye, Min Huang, Tao Pu, Tan Qin, Huaiyuan Zhou, Yushuo Liu

title: Explicit Semantic Transition Modeling for Open-Vocabulary Remote Sensing Change Detection
content: Open-vocabulary change detection (OVCD) aims to detect land-cover changes associated with semantic concepts, but existing methods usually infer change semantics from independently predicted endpoint labels. Such endpoint-centric formulations do not directly model semantic change as a directed from-to transition and may suffer from accumulated endpoint errors. In this article, we propose an explicit semantic transition modeling framework for open-vocabulary remote sensing change detection. The proposed method uses frozen DINOv2 and SegEarth-OV3 to extract bi-temporal visual features, semantic probability maps, and text prototypes. A lightweight proposal branch identifies ROIs that may contain changes, within which the model directly predicts pixel-level directed semantic transitions. To handle the large transition space, a compact Top- $k$  candidate set is first constructed from ROI semantic distributions, and a residual candidate supplement module (RCSM) further supplements potentially omitted transitions. Moreover, a consistency-aware semantic transition refinement module (CSTRM) calibrates transition logits through transition-marginal consistency (TMC) and improves spatial coherence through transition-aware refinement. Experiments on six remote sensing change detection datasets demonstrate that the proposed formulation consistently outperforms representative unsupervised, foundation-model-based, and open-vocabulary methods. The code will be available at https://github.com/liuyk97/OV-SCD
author: Yikun Liu, Ying Li, Zhihao Li, Minghao Liu, Gongping Yang

title: Soil Knowledge-Guided Depth-Autoregressive Transformer for Predicting Soil Organic Carbon at Multiple Depths
content: The soil organic carbon (SOC) is a critical component of the terrestrial carbon cycle and a key indicator of soil health and agricultural productivity. The accurate prediction of SOC across multiple depths is essential for reliable carbon stock estimation and sustainable soil management. However, the existing approaches still face challenges in achieving high accuracy for deep SOC prediction and often lack the incorporation of soil knowledge, leading to limited model stability, especially for deep soils. To address these issues, we proposed a depth-autoregressive transformer that enhances depth representation through optimized depth embeddings and leverages autoregressive prediction to incorporate prior SOC information from adjacent layers. In addition, a soil knowledge-guided loss (SKG-Loss) was introduced, integrating depth constraints and feature monotonicity constraints to guide the training process. A total of 256 soil cores (0–100 cm) were collected and divided into four depth intervals (0–20, 20–40, 40–60, and 60–100 cm) in this study. Based on multisource environmental covariates, a multitemporal feature set with 32 predictors was developed. The results from location-based fivefold cross-validation demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms five commonly used models, achieving an R2 of 0.69, a root mean square error (RMSE) of 4.11 g kg−1, and a mean absolute error (MAE) of 3.03 g kg−1. The incorporation of SKG-Loss consistently improves prediction accuracy across all depths, with particularly notable gains at 20–60 cm (approximately 10% increase in R ${}^{2}$ ). Finally, the SOC distribution maps at multiple depths with 10-m spatial resolution were generated for the study area. Overall, the proposed approach improves both the accuracy and stability of depthwise SOC prediction, providing an effective and physically informed framework for 3-D SOC mapping and carbon stock assessment.
author: Rui Lu, Hancheng Guo, Zhongxing Chen, Tieming Chen, Zhou Shi, Songchao Chen

title: 3-D Inversion of Loop-Source Semiairborne Transient Electromagnetic Data Incorporating Topographic Effects
content: Semiairborne transient electromagnetics (SATEMs) is an emerging geophysical method for mineral exploration, hydrogeological investigations, and engineering applications owing to its high resolution for shallow targets and strong sensitivity to conductive bodies. However, the inherent nonuniqueness of conventional 1-D inversion, together with response distortions induced by topography, can significantly degrade the accuracy and resolution of loop-source SATEM imaging. To address these issues, we develop a 3-D forward and inversion framework that explicitly incorporates topographic effects for SATEM data interpretation. The forward solver uses an unstructured vector finite-element (FE) formulation coupled with an unconditionally stable, second-order backward Euler (SBE) time-stepping scheme, enabling high-fidelity simulations overrugged surfaces. The inversion is accelerated using a limited-memory BFGS algorithm, substantially reducing the computational cost and memory demands associated with sensitivity calculations. Synthetic experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach accurately recovers the geometry and resistivity of subsurface anomalies, and that incorporating topography markedly improves boundary delineation. We further assess the method using two geologically realistic benchmark models: a geological–geophysical model from the Eagle Mountain Mine (USA) and a borehole-constrained model from Voisey’s Bay (Canada).
author: Siyuan Zhang, Junjie Xie, Xinyu Wang, Ri Wang, Siyi Lan, Hongzhu Cai, Xiangyun Hu

title: A Deep Learning Framework for Angular Resolution Enhancement of Multichannel Forward-Looking SAR Under Space-Variant and Perturbed Kernels
content: With multiple channels resolving left/right ambiguity, multichannel synthetic aperture radar (SAR) has the ability to perform forward-looking imaging. However, its angular resolution, especially in regions close to the flight path, is limited by the aperture size. In this article, an enhanced imaging scheme under space-variant and perturbed kernels for multichannel forward-looking SAR is proposed. In the scheme, the ideal space-variant convolution matrix is obtained first with the provided system parameters. Then, the linear mapping equation between the preliminary imaging result and the scene is established. The alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) is adopted to solve the optimization problem, and the procedure is unrolled into network form. Meanwhile, to overcome the influence of nonideal factors such as residual errors and noise, the influence of a perturbed kernel function is considered by introducing a perturbation factor and synchronously estimating it during iterations, and the plug-and-play (PnP) module with denoising is added to the network. At last, the experimental results are illustrated to verify the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.
author: Wenchao Li, Chengjie Kang, Genghao Zhang, Rui Chen, Junjie Wu, Jianyu Yang

title: A Spaceborne SAR RFI Suppression Method Based on an Adaptive Subband-Forming Technology
content: Radio frequency interference (RFI) severely degrades the quality of spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images. The most current methods usually mitigate interference in only a single domain, such as notch filtering (NF) in the frequency domain, beamforming (BF) in the spatial domain, or low-rank and sparse methods in the energy domain. Inspired by BF techniques, this article designs an adaptive subband-forming technology (SFT) model that combines both the frequency and energy domains (EDs) for interference suppression. The proposed technology consists of two processing modes: the model-solving SFT (MS-SFT) mode and the weight-application SFT (WA-SFT) mode. By introducing spectrum division into a low-rank optimization model, the model can be solved by the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) with closed-form updates, and then a signal component, an RFI component, and a set of optimal subband weights can be obtained from the raw polluted SAR data. After solving the proposed model, the optimal subband weights can be applied directly to reconstruct the clean scenes and mitigate the homologous interference (HI) with similar spectral characteristics in other regions without iteration, by using the WA-SFT algorithm. Experiments on Sentinel-1 C-band data and LuTan-1 L-band data demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed MS-SFT and WA-SFT modes.
author: Xuezhi Chen, Yan Huang, Xutao Yu, Jie Li, Yuan Mao, Shuyi Gu, Yanyang Liu, Zaichen Zhang

title: PC-MTPNet With Prototype Constraints for Fine-Grained Rice Classification From Multi-Temporal Polarimetric SAR Images
content: Multi-temporal polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (SAR) captures temporal dynamics and polarimetric scattering variations during the rice-growing season, providing critical information for crop growth monitoring and fine-grained rice classification. However, in complex SAR backgrounds, rice fields are often surrounded by water, shoals, and urban built-up areas, while speckle noise and mixed boundaries further hinder accurate fine-grained discrimination. Existing deep segmentation networks typically feed SAR features directly into the model, with limited explicit modeling of the statistical structure of multi-temporal polarimetric features and fine-grained rice categories. They also lack effective constraints on intraclass compactness and interclass separability, leading to substantial confusion between rice subcategories. To address these limitations, this study proposes PC-MTPNet for fine-grained rice classification using multi-temporal full- and compact-polarimetric SAR features. PC-MTPNet integrates the multi-temporal polarimetric statistical descriptor (MTP-Desc), the multi-temporal polarimetric prototype constraint (MTP-Polar), and a detail-refined U-Net++ backbone. A composite loss function is introduced to impose intraclass compactness and interclass separation, while an edge head, boundary loss, and Hann–Gaussian sliding-window fusion are employed to enhance boundary delineation and full-scene inference stability. Experimental results show that PC-MTPNet achieves an overall accuracy (OA), mean intersection over union (mIoU), macro-averaged  $F1$  score (Macro-F1), and Kappa of 93.73%, 86.49%, 92.66%, and 92.11%, respectively. Compared with U-Net++, SegFormer-B1, CVNN-PolSAR, and other methods, PC-MTPNet improves these four metrics by at least 3.05, 5.11, 2.80, and 0.55 percentage points, with maximum gains of 11.80, 19.40, 12.83, and 14.72 percentage points, respectively. For direct-sown japonica rice paddy (D-J) and transplanted hybrid rice paddy (T-H), PC-MTPNet achieves classification accuracies of 93.50% and 92.49%, respectively, improving over the U-Net++ baseline by 17.57 and 16.50 percentage points, respectively. These results indicate that multi-temporal polarimetric statistical description and prototype constraints effectively reduce statistical confusion between rice subcategories and improve the robustness of fine-grained rice classification in complex polarimetric SAR scenes.
author: Xianyu Guo, Junming Liang, Junjun Yin, Kun Li, Jian Yang

title: Ground Moving Target Detection in Multichannel Polarization SAR-GMTI Systems
content: In this article, a novel ground moving target (GMT) detection algorithm is proposed in a synthetic aperture radar (SAR) system based on the space–time-polarization cascaded processing. In the proposed method, the polarization classification is first accomplished based on multipolarization data, followed by spatial domain adaptive processing in the SAR image domain for each polarization channel based on the polarization classification results. Subsequently, the preliminary detection results of moving targets from a single polarization channel can be obtained, and the target polarization steering vectors can be estimated through an iterative process, in order to achieve adaptive coherent synthesis of the target signal in the polarization domain and accomplish the secondary clutter cancellation. Furthermore, a target detection technique based on the polarization distance window detector (PD-DT) is proposed to effectively enhance the detection probability of moving targets and decrease false alarms. Finally, based on the estimated polarization steering vectors of GMTs, adaptive processing in the polarization domain is performed for each spatial channel, greatly improving the output signal-to-clutter-plus-noise ratios (SCNRs) for detected targets, beneficial to the subsequent target relocation. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified using real-measured data from an airborne multichannel fully polarimetric SAR (Pol-SAR) system.
author: Penghui Huang, Junjie Li, Lingyu Wang, Jixia Fan, Jingtao Ma, Jingxian Chen, Yanyang Liu, Guisheng Liao

title: Electro-Optical Response-Aware Learning for PAN-Sharpening of Satellite Images
content: Most deep-learning-based panchromatic (PAN)-sharpening methods are trained under simplified and fixed degradation models, typically assuming an isotropic Gaussian point spread function (PSF). However, real electro-optical (EO) satellite systems exhibit scene- and acquisition-dependent blur characteristics caused by diffraction, optical aberrations, platform motion, and intersensor misalignment, which results in a domain gap between synthetic training data and real-world observations. To narrow this gap, we analyze satellite star images and observe that the effective blur is often anisotropic and exhibits extended non-Gaussian residuals. Based on this observation, we propose a PSF prediction network (PSFPN) that estimates a scene-specific PSF consisting of an anisotropic Gaussian component and a residual term. The predicted PSFs quantitatively reveal sensor-dependent EO responses: the mean anisotropy ratios are 1.012, 1.310, and 1.041 for Korea Multi-Purpose Satellite-3A (KOMPSAT-3A), WorldView-II, and QuickBird, respectively. We then use the predicted PSFs to generate physically consistent training data for existing PAN-sharpening networks without changing their inference architectures. To evaluate the effectiveness of our PSFPN, we conducted comparative experiments on four deep-learning-based PAN-sharpening methods trained with fixed PSF-based and PSFPN-based degradation processes. Extensive experiments on multiple satellite datasets show that the PAN-sharpening methods trained with PSFPN-based degradation outperform those trained with fixed PSF-based degradation in both reduced- and full-resolution evaluations, while also enhancing geometric consistency and reducing misregistration-related artifacts. In particular, under the PSFPN-based degradation test protocol, the average peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) values of the four deep-learning-based PAN-sharpening methods trained with our PSFPN-based degradation are higher than those trained with a fixed PSF by 0.6970, 0.9158, and 1.0432 dB on the KOMPSAT-3A, WorldView-II, and QuickBird datasets, respectively. Under the random anisotropic Gaussian-based degradation test protocol, the corresponding average PSNR improvements on the KOMPSAT-3A, WorldView-II, and QuickBird datasets are 0.5058, 0.4900, and 0.5037 dB, respectively, without any additional inference cost.
author: Hyun-Ho Kim, Munchurl Kim

title: Weakly Supervised Hyperspectral Target Detection Based on Contrastive Learning and Graph-Structural Position
content: Hyperspectral target detection is significant in remote sensing, yet existing methods heavily rely on strong supervision. Target prior spectra are sensitive to illumination, atmospheric, and sensor variations, causing inevitable deviations that degrade performance. Pixel-level annotations are prohibitively costly due to high spatial resolution and subpixel localization difficulties. Multiple instance learning enables weakly supervised detection using region-level labels, but most existing methods neglect spatial dependencies among pixels and suffer from limited localization capability. To address these issues, this article proposes a graph-structured positional transformer for multiple-instance learning (GSPT-MIL), a graph-structured and position-aware weakly supervised multiple-instance learning (MIL) method that achieves accurate pixel-level detection using only bag-level labels, without requiring target priors or pixel-level annotations. The method performs iterative optimization under an expectation-maximization (EM) framework. The expectation step (E-step) infers target locations via a local similarity graph convolution module (LS-GCM) that models spatial dependencies, while the maximization step (M-step) fuses absolute position information via a multiscale contextual position encoder and enhances feature discriminability via a spectral–spatial feature alignment network (SS-FAN). Extensive experiments demonstrate that GSPT-MIL consistently outperforms existing weakly supervised and conventional detection methods, validating its effectiveness and superiority.
author: Ying Cui, Xiaoqi Ren, Liguo Wang, Haifeng Zhu, Zhongwei Shen, Chunhui Zhao

title: Reconstructing Multiangular Field HCRF Spectra From Indoor Measurements via a Spectral–Frequency–Global Network
content: Recovering physically consistent reflectance from spectra affected by systematic measurement errors remains a fundamental challenge in quantitative remote sensing, especially when the observation process is only partially modeled. In indoor semiphysical, multiangular measurement systems, residual discrepancies persist between indoor hemispherical-conical reflectance factor (HCRF) measurements and outdoor field observations because of illumination mismatch, geometric uncertainty, and instrument-induced spectral distortions. To address this problem, this article formulates indoor-to-field correction as an angle-aware spectral reconstruction task and proposes a data-driven framework termed the spectral–frequency–global network (SFGNet). The network jointly models local spectral features, long-range spectral dependencies, frequency-domain residual patterns, and observation geometry, enabling the correction of both radiometric bias and spectral-shape distortion under anisotropic conditions. Extensive experiments on paired indoor–outdoor HCRF measurements of multiple mineral samples show that, compared with raw indoor observations, SFGNet directly reduces the average mean squared error (mse) by 75.4% and increases the spectral correlation coefficient (SCC) from 0.9024 to 0.9595. Further analyses demonstrate improved angular anisotropy reconstruction and robust spatiotemporal generalization to independent field samples. These results demonstrate that geometry-aware data-driven correction effectively enhances the field consistency of indoor HCRF measurements and supports high-accuracy optical remote sensing simulation.
author: Guorui Jia, Honglin Ji, Huijie Zhao, Feixiang Wang, Zhen Li, Xianfei Qiu, Xiaoshuang Wu, Yinuo Wang

title: Hardness-Aware Contrastive Learning With Data Condensation for Open-Set Hyperspectral Image Classification
content: In recent years, hyperspectral image classification (HSIC) has been widely applied in precision agriculture, environmental monitoring, and remote sensing. However, the frequent emergence of unknown categories, such as novel land-cover types and anomalous regions, poses significant challenges to traditional closed-set classifiers. Open-set classification seeks to accurately recognize known classes while rejecting unknown ones, but existing methods are often limited by high intraclass spectral variability, insufficient exploitation of hard samples, and imprecise class representations. To overcome these challenges, this article proposes an open-set detection framework called HACL-DC, which combines hardness-aware contrastive learning with soft-label-weighted data condensation. The framework consists of three key components. First, a similarity contrastive weighting module enhances contrastive learning by assigning higher weights to hard intraclass positives and interclass negatives through linear transformations combined with sigmoid and inverse-sigmoid functions, promoting compact intraclass features and stronger interclass separation. Second, a soft-label-weighted condensation algorithm (SWCA) constructs compact etalon sets for each known class by leveraging soft-label assignment, dual-parameter gradient optimization, and adaptive etalon resetting to capture fine-grained class distributions and local density information. Finally, weighted similarities between test samples and class etalons are computed using etalon influence scores, enabling accurate known-class classification and effective detection of out-of-distribution (OOD) samples. Extensive experiments on three public hyperspectral datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed HACL-DC framework.
author: Hanyue Wang, Wei Liu, Jing Zhao, Xianghai Cao, Licheng Jiao

title: WF-Mamba: Weighted Fourier State-Space Models With Adaptive Spatial-Frequency Synergy for Hyperspectral Unmixing
content: Hyperspectral unmixing (HU) is a crucial technique that aims to estimate subpixel-level ground object information in remote sensing images. Existing deep learning-based unmixing methods, especially autoencoders (AEs), typically operate only within the original spatial–spectral feature domain. However, due to the impact of noise and spectral variability, relying solely on the original domain makes it difficult to fully extract effective features and leaves the models highly susceptible to interference. To address these issues, we present an innovative dual-stream spatial-frequency state-space model (SSM), termed WF-Mamba, for enhanced HU. A physics-driven snake-like scanning (SS) mechanism is introduced in WF-Mamba to remodel the data serialization process, which strictly preserves the intrinsic neighborhood contiguity and 2-D topological priors. To extend the feature domain and overcome the frequency-domain blindness of pure spatial models, a macroscopic weighted Fourier neural operator (WFNO) branch is constructed. By dynamically recalibrating global low-frequency modes in the complex domain, WFNO functions as an advanced physical filter to actively suppress high-frequency noise. Furthermore, an adaptive synergistic fusion (ASF) mechanism is proposed for WF-Mamba to break the bottleneck of rigid feature concatenation. More robust features can be obtained by ASF by autonomously balancing the sharp local spatial boundaries extracted by Mamba with the globally purified smoothness from WFNO via dynamic residual gating. The fused robust features are then mapped to estimate accurate abundances and reconstruct the image. Extensive experiments on one synthetic and three real hyperspectral datasets demonstrate that the proposed WF-Mamba achieves competitive performance compared to advanced methods.
author: Lianhui Liang, Jinrong Chen, Shaoquan Zhang, Bing Tu, Jun Li, Antonio Plaza

title: DDFGFormer: Dual-Decoupled Frequency-Guided Transformer for Hyperspectral Image Classification
content: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification requires jointly capturing subtle spectral differences and complex spatial structures. Recent studies have introduced frequency-domain modeling to complement spatial–spectral representation learning. However, existing frequency-based methods still face some limitations. First, most methods mainly focus on amplitude or energy distributions while insufficiently exploiting phase information for structural localization and edge representation. In addition, raw phase information is sensitive to noise, smooth regions, and mixed pixels, which may introduce unreliable interference. Furthermore, spatial–frequency interaction is often implemented through simple posterior fusion, failing to use frequency-domain priors to actively guide spatial feature extraction. To address these limitations, we propose a dual-decoupled frequency-guided transformer, termed DDFGFormer, for HSI classification. In particular, we design a frequency-guided transformer block (FGTB) composed of dual-decoupled frequency attention (DDFA) and a frequency-enhanced feed-forward network (FEFFN). DDFA decouples the Fourier representation into amplitude and phase, and further decomposes the amplitude into high- and low-frequency components, thereby explicitly capturing amplitude- and phase-aware cues. To suppress unreliable phase responses, an amplitude-prior guided phase (APGP) module contained in DDFA is proposed to adaptively modulate phase representations and transform raw phase into stable structural priors. Furthermore, FEFFN injects frequency-domain information into feature propagation, enabling frequency priors to actively recalibrate spatial features rather than serving only as posterior fusion cues. Extensive experiments on four HSI datasets show that DDFGFormer outperforms nine state-of-the-art methods in overall accuracy (OA), average accuracy (AA), kappa, and boundary  $F1$ -score (BF1), with OA gains of 1.65%, 1.63%, 1.25%, and 1.14% over the second-best method on Indian Pines (IPs), Pavia University (PU), Salinas (SAs), and WHU-Hi-LongKou (LK), respectively.
author: Jinliang An, Dengru Han, Longlong Dai, Weidong Zhang, Xiangrong Zhang

title: GeoSelect: Spatial-Program Execution for Training-Free Referring Remote Sensing Image Segmentation
content: Referring remote sensing image segmentation (RRSIS) segments the object named by a natural-language expression in an aerial image. Existing training-free methods resolve the expression through implicit vision–language activations or region–text similarity, which gives weak control over the spatial, superlative, and ordinal relations that dominate aerial referring, such as the rightmost ship or the second court from the left. We propose GeoSelect, a training-free pipeline that reframes referring as the execution of a typed spatial program. A frozen, text-only language model synthesizes the expression into a small domain-specific language (DSL), a well-formedness checker accepts the program, and a deterministic executor runs it. The central abstraction is a single scored candidate set type under which every operator composes: continuous geometric fields realize position and proximity, while discrete set and order operators add the extremum, ordinal, top- $k$ , and relational constructions that fields alone cannot express. Execution is explicit, so every intermediate is inspectable, and a reliability ladder degrades any failing program to the field-only special case. GeoSelect achieves 58.86 mIoU on RRSIS-D test and 55.27 mIoU on RISBench test, more than twice the best prior training-free method on RRSIS-D, with no referring supervision and on a single GPU. Under a fixed detector and segmenter, explicit execution improves over implicit selectors under the same backbone; the best-box-IoU and outcome-partition diagnostics motivate complementary tests of proposal recall and program-path behavior, with the program path the clearer priority on RISBench, and an exposure audit shows comparable accuracy on the audited unseen subset. Code and configurations are available at https://github.com/Avalon-S/GeoSelect
author: Yuhang Jiang, Guohui Deng, Miaozhong Xu, Chao Ruan, Jinling Zhao, Linsheng Huang

title: BCAP: Black-Box Cross-Modal Adversarial Patch Attacks Against Multimodal Vehicle Recognition Systems via UAV Remote Sensing
content: The reliability of deep learning-based object detection in uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) remote sensing increasingly relies on fusing visible and infrared sensors. However, existing attack methods used to evaluate their robustness are often unrealistic, assuming white-box access or targeting only a single modality. This article first reveals a critical cross-modal vulnerability through region sensitivity analysis on various YOLO detectors, demonstrating that both visible and infrared models exhibit a shared spatial weakness by being most sensitive to perturbations in the target vehicle’s central area. Leveraging this key insight, we propose a framework with black-box cross-modal adversarial patch (BCAP) attacks on UAV detectors. BCAP introduces a multiobjective optimization formulation that models visible and infrared modalities as independent yet competing objectives, which enables effective cross-modal optimization without manual weight tuning. It employs a novel grid-constrained Bezier curve generation method to efficiently search for smooth, effective patch shapes within this sensitive central region, further enhanced by an adaptive population restart strategy. Extensive experiments on the DroneVehicle dataset show BCAP achieves a 50%–61% cross-modal attack success rate (ASR), significantly outperforming the 37%–42% range of existing methods. This work provides a more potent and realistic baseline for evaluating the end-to-end reliability of multimodal UAV remote sensing systems.
author: Jiayi Wang, Hua Han, Kaiyu Xu, Li Huang

title: Scale-Consistent Multispectral Reconstruction From UAV and Satellite Observations for Coastal Bathymetric Inversion
content: High-resolution quantitative remote sensing is constrained by the spatial–spectral trade-off among current observation platforms: uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery provides fine spatial detail but limited spectral dimensionality, whereas satellite multispectral data provide richer spectral information at coarser spatial scales. This study proposes data-driven spectral-structural anchoring fusion (DSSAF), a scale-consistent framework that reconstructs UAV-scale multispectral imagery by integrating fine-resolution structural information from UAV RGB imagery with multispectral constraints from PlanetScope observations. The framework combines land-cover-conditioned spectral mapping, data-driven structural reference selection, adaptive detail injection, and scale-consistency correction. It was evaluated over a heterogeneous intertidal sandbar system and further tested through shallow-water bathymetric inversion. The reconstructed imagery preserved UAV-scale textures, gradients, and edges while remaining radiometrically consistent with the original PlanetScope data after reaggregation to the native satellite scale. In the downstream bathymetry task, DSSAF-fused imagery achieved the best performance among the tested inputs, with R ${}^{2} =0.924$  and RMSE = 0.079 m. These results demonstrate that scale-consistent UAV-satellite fusion can improve both image-level spatial–spectral representation and quantitative geophysical retrieval, providing a transferable approach for high-resolution environmental mapping in heterogeneous coastal landscapes.
author: Jianchun Chen, Ya Ping Wang, Yan Gu, Shibing Zhu, Chao Gao, Renzhi Li

title: AMS-SemiCD: A Synergistic Framework for Semisupervised Change Detection via an Adaptive Pseudolabeling Strategy and a Multibranch Network
content: Semisupervised change detection (SSCD) aims to reduce the dependence on extensive labeled data. However, existing methods face three critical challenges. First, class imbalance and boundary ambiguity induce class-dependent confidence distributions, hindering reliable pseudolabel selection. Second, uncertain pixels may still contain useful structural cues, while their indiscriminate use can amplify pseudolabel noise. Third, achieving complementary local–global feature representations in dual-branch architectures typically incurs prohibitive computational costs. To address these issues, we propose the adaptive multibranch synergistic SSCD (AMS-SemiCD) framework, which uses teacher–student consistency regularization to supervise unlabeled bitemporal pairs. Within this framework, the adaptive statistical pseudolabel refinement (ASPR) strategy improves the reliability and utilization of consistency targets through class-adaptive dynamic thresholding and contribution-adaptive soft weighting. As a result, ASPR accommodates class-dependent confidence distributions while effectively exploiting uncertain but informative pixels. Meanwhile, the multibranch synergistic enhancement network (MSE-Net) enhances discriminative feature representation by integrating local CNN and global Mamba branches with manageable computational costs. Specifically, MSE-Net consists of the multibranch spatiotemporal synergistic fusion (MSSF) for local–global fusion, the multibranch spatiotemporal difference booster (MSDB) for temporal-difference enhancement, and the adaptive gated attention refiner (AGAR) for cross-layer refinement. Extensive experiments on the GoogleGZ-CD, WHU-CD, and LEVIR-CD datasets demonstrate that AMS-SemiCD consistently outperforms advanced SSCD methods. Notably, with only 20% labeled data on LEVIR-CD, our method achieves an  $F1$  score of 91.17% and an intersection over union (IoU) of 83.78%. The code will be available at https://github.com/RSII-NWNUAMS-SemiCD
author: Di Zhang, Peicheng Yue, Huifang Ma, Zhanjun Hao, Xin He, Yun Liu, Jiaqi Zhao

title: A Growth-Prior-Informed Forest Age Estimation Method Using Overlapping ICESat/GLAS and GEDI Footprints With Reduced Dependence on Field Calibration Data
content: Forest age is a critical ecological variable for quantifying carbon sequestration, assessing biodiversity, and supporting sustainable forest management. Conventional remote sensing approaches for forest age estimation either rely heavily on field inventory data or require long-term optical archives, limiting their scalability and applicability across diverse forest types and age ranges. This study presented a novel light detection and ranging (LiDAR)-based framework that leverages the temporal complementarity of the Ice, Cloud, and land Elevation Satellite/Geoscience Laser Altimeter System (ICESat/GLAS, 2003–2009) and the Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI, 2019-present). By reformulating classical height-age growth models into a temporally paired-height structure, canopy height at the later observation was expressed as a function of canopy height at the earlier observation and the elapsed time interval. Overlapping GLAS and GEDI footprints provide paired canopy height observations spanning more than a decade, enabling direct parameterization of growth models with reduced dependence on field-derived age calibration data. The framework was evaluated in two ecologically distinct regions. For Larix gmelinii in Northeast China, the estimated ages achieved an R2 of 0.86 with a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 13.37 years. For loblolly pine in the southeastern United States, the corresponding R2 and RMSE were 0.71 and 5.74 years, respectively. Further simulations with random height measurement errors confirmed the resilience of the model, demonstrating strong robustness for loblolly pine and relative stability for L. gmelinii, with increased sensitivity only in later growth stages. Building on these results, the models were applied at the regional scale to generate 30 m resolution forest age maps for both study areas. At the regional scale, the estimated mean age in Study Area I was 55.8 years, broadly consistent with the estimates from two independent national products (59.6 and 64.5 years), and the young-forest proportion was 16.4%. In Study Area II, map-derived ages showed strong agreement with stand-level observations (R ${}^{2} =0.96$ , RMSE = 2.83 years). Overall, this LiDAR-driven framework substantially reduces dependence on dense field calibration and long-term optical time series, offering a complementary pathway for full-spectrum forest age estimation.
author: Yiya Qiao, Sheng Nie, Cheng Wang, Xiaohuan Xi

title: Residual Multiple Suppression Using a Physics-Informed Plug-In Network With Residual-Multiple-Level Prior
content: Multiple suppression is a fundamental problem in seismic processing because residual multiples often exhibit kinematic characteristics similar to those of primary reflections, making these interfering events hard to remove cleanly in practice. As a result, conventional methods usually face a tradeoff: aggressive parameter settings tend to damage useful primaries, whereas conservative settings often leave residual multiple energy insufficiently attenuated. To address this issue, this article presents a physics-informed plug-in network for residual multiple suppression. Instead of replacing conventional demultiple pipelines, the proposed method takes preliminary demultiple results as input and performs targeted refinement on the remaining residual multiples. The framework first estimates a physics-guided residual-multiple-level prior to characterize the spatial distribution of residual contamination. This prior then guides an attention-based attenuation network to apply spatially varying suppression strength. In addition, an optional geological-structure-guided recovery step can further return primary-consistent energy from the removed component. For training, samples are adaptively synthesized from real-data-derived primary and residual-multiple proxies. In this way, the method preserves compatibility with existing industrial workflows while improving the balance between residual attenuation and primary preservation. Experiments on synthetic and field data show that the proposed method suppresses residual multiple energy more effectively than conventional baselines while better preserving the continuity and amplitude consistency of primary reflections.
author: Zhiyu Yao, Wenkai Lu, Weiheng Geng, Jinpeng Liu, Mingrui Zhong, Yili Ren

title: Adaptive-Dictionary-Regularized 3-D Direct Inversion of Surface-Wave Dispersion Data
content: Conventional global smoothing regularization suppresses velocity anomaly amplitudes and blurs structural boundaries in regions of sparse ray coverage, limiting fine-scale crustal imaging under nonuniform observational conditions. This study introduces local sparse regularization based on adaptive-dictionary learning into the DSurfTomo 3-D direct inversion framework, yielding the DSurfTomo-local sparse tomography (LST) method, which simultaneously characterizes smooth velocity backgrounds and discontinuous structural boundaries. Under a Bayesian maximum a posteriori (MAP) formulation, the method couples the global  $L_{2}$  constraint and a local dictionary sparsity prior in a unified objective function and jointly solves for the velocity model and sparse coefficients via alternating minimization. During the inversion iterations, dictionary atoms are updated in synchrony with the velocity model using the iterative thresholding and signed K-means (ITKM) algorithm, ensuring that the sparsity regularization remains consistent with the local structure of the current velocity field throughout the inversion. Synthetic data tests demonstrate that, relative to DSurfTomo, DSurfTomo-LST significantly improves velocity anomaly amplitude recovery and structural-boundary resolution under sparse ray-coverage conditions, with the overall root-mean-square error (RMSE) reduced by approximately 38% and 22% in the checkerboard and spike tests, respectively. Applications to the ChinArray data recover velocity structures consistent with regional tectonic features. The Luzhou dense-array results show velocity anomalies whose spatial distribution broadly corresponds to structural features observed in the seismic reflection profile.
author: Zhiwen Li, Jianyang Ding, Xiaoyan Cheng, Renjie He, Xiaohua Zhou, Zubin Chen

title: A Simplified Analysis of Full-Waveform Inversion (FWI) With Optimal Transport
content: Full-waveform inversion (FWI) is a key seismic imaging method, posed as a nonlinear optimization problem to recover high-resolution subsurface models. Its usual least-squares ( $L^{2}$ ) misfit, however, often converges to local minima because of the objective’s strong nonconvexity and cycle skipping. To mitigate this, recent work explores optimal transport (OT)-based misfits, particularly the squared Wasserstein-2 distance ( $W_{2}^{2}$ ), which has better convexity properties. This article analytically characterizes this metric by deriving a simplified 1-D expression for the gradient of  $W_{2}^{2}$  under assumptions relevant to early-stage FWI. This enables a direct quantitative comparison between  $W_{2}^{2}$  and  $L^{2}$  gradients and clarifies the theoretical advantages of the Wasserstein metric for estimating acoustic velocity in homogeneous regions, improving FWI robustness and efficiency.
author: Cristhian Alberto Celestino Cortez, Djalma Manoel Soares Filho, Lucas Gondim Miranda, Maria Clara Godinho Ciloni, Eduardo Parente Ribeiro

title: Integrating Multisource Observations for Spatiotemporal Subsidence Monitoring and Constrained High-precision Reservoir Parameter Inversion in the Shuguang Oilfield
content: Long-term deformation monitoring and high-precision reservoir parameter inversion are essential for mitigating geohazards and ensuring production safety in oilfield regions. This study utilizes Sentinel-1A imagery from 2017 to 2025 and employs the small baseline subset interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) technology to reveal the spatiotemporal evolution of land subsidence in the Shuguang Oilfield. The results identify a maximum cumulative deformation of 120 cm and a peak subsidence rate of –12 cm/yr, which are rigorously validated by high-precision ground monitoring data. By integrating unmanned aerial vehicle digital orthophoto maps, the spatial damage effects of differential subsidence on critical infrastructure are accurately quantified. To overcome the geometric blind spots and nonuniqueness inherent in single line of sight InSAR inversions for anisotropic reservoirs, a “Model-Ground” joint inversion framework is proposed by incorporating high-precision ground observations. This framework utilizes 3-D surface displacements as hard constraints in Bayesian inference, significantly narrowing the prior search space for reservoir parameters. Quantitative evaluation demonstrates that this joint constraint reduces the residual variance of the Sill model by approximately 65% and achieves an uncertainty reduction rate of up to 59% for deep dynamic parameters. The established multisource synergistic monitoring and high-fidelity inversion paradigm effectively decouples the bias between subsurface stress fields and geometric parameters, providing robust scientific support for geohazard early warning and the sustainable development of complex oil and gas reservoirs with highly compressible overburdens.
author: Zhen Li, Minghui Wang, Shuangcheng Zhang, Bo Lian, Bo Yao, Yan Wang, Yanhao Li, Ning Liu, Yuhui Wei, Xinyi Xue

title: TS-DeShadowNet: A Two-Stage Remote Sensing Image Shadow Removal Method
content: Shadow removal for remote sensing images is a challenging task. Mask-based methods require prohibitively expensive pixel-level shadow mask annotation, while mask-free methods suffer from a domain gap between rigorously consistent paired shadow and shadow-free images. Moreover, the shadow removal on large-scale remote sensing images induces heavy computation and inefficient long-range modeling. To address these issues, we propose TS-DeShadowNet, a novel two-stage framework encompassing a wavelet transform and Mamba-based diffusion network (WMDNet) and a style transfer-based image radiometric quality enhancement network (STENet). The WMDNet performs mask-free shadow removal through a dual-branch diffusion model equipped with wavelet transform and Mamba. It explicitly decouples the image into the low-frequency and high-frequency components and jointly optimizes the dual branches for global illumination recovery and local texture restoration. In addition, the WMDNet also introduces the Mamba-based denoising encoder–decoder to model multidirectional long-range spatial dependencies with linear complexity. The STENet formulates the image radiometric quality enhancement as a self-referenced style transfer task. By extracting authentic statistical priors directly from the shadow-free regions of the shadow image and injecting them via dynamic affine transformations, STENet effectively mitigates the impact of the domain gap. Extensive experiments on the UAV-SC and SRGTA datasets demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method in removing image shadows and enhancing image radiometric quality.
author: Hongliang Ji, Chenguang Dai, Qi Dong, Wenke Li, Li Li, Kangrui Li, Hanyun Wang

title: A Geospatial–Spectral Image Fusion Framework Guided by Deep Reinforcement Learning-Selected Key Information for Forest Aboveground Carbon Stock Estimation
content: Accurate estimation of forest aboveground carbon stock (AGC) is essential for carbon governance, but potential geospatial correlations may affect estimation accuracy. Although hyperspectral imaging (HSI) remote sensing can characterize vegetation changes caused by geospatial differences, its redundancy hinders models from capturing geospatial information. To this end, a key information-guided geospatial–spectral image fusion framework (KIG-GeoSIF) is proposed to improve the model's ability to capture geospatial information while reducing HSI redundancy. First, a multiagent (MA) key information selection module, MA-S$^{2}$-MMS-PPO, is designed based on proximal policy optimization (PPO). It fuses spectral–spatial (S$^{2}$) correlation features extracted from Gramian angular field (GAF)-encoded images with historical actions to construct a multimodal state representation (MMS), and incorporates an efficiency-oriented composite reward mechanism to guide multiple agents in differentially selecting AGC-sensitive bands. Then, they are input into the GC-bidirectional cross-attention fusion (BCAF) module, which integrates geospatial features from the graph attention network and spectral image features from the convolutional neural network (CNN) through BCAF. In the methodological validation experiment, the spectral branch constructed from the 42 bands selected by MA-S$^{2}$-MMS-PPO achieved the best performance (mean five-fold R$^{2}$ = 0.7394), while fixed-band-number comparisons further verified the effectiveness of the MMS-based MA mechanism. Furthermore, using the 46 key bands selected exclusively based on the modeling set, GC-BCAF achieved R$^{2}=0.8348$ on the independent spatial test set. KIG-GeoSIF enhances geospatial information utilization through key-band guidance to improve AGC estimation, providing scientific support for carbon governance.
author: Qiang Liu, Jiawei Zhang, Zhaoxing Li, Ying'ao Jiao, Meiting Zhao, Chunmei Yang, Xuemei Guan, Jianping Huang

title: Hybrid SNN-Transformer Network With Membrane-Potential-Aware Attention for Hyperspectral Image Classification
content: Vision Transformers (ViTs) achieve high accuracy in hyperspectral image classification (HSIC) yet incur prohibitive computational cost, hindering edge deployment. Spiking neural networks (SNNs) promise energy-efficient event-driven computation, but directly transferring ViTs to SNNs leads to severe information loss from binary spikes, which is further amplified under the extremely limited labeled samples typical of HSIC. To address these intertwined challenges, we propose a spiking grouped separable convolutional vision transformer (Spiking-GSCViT) featuring a novel membrane-potential-aware grouped self-attention (MPA-GSA) module. MPA-GSA calculates attention weights from continuous, differentiable membrane potentials, rather than from lossy binary spikes. Moreover, leveraging the time-varying nature of membrane potentials, this novel attention mechanism is able to attend to different spectral–spatial regions across multiple time steps, thereby preserving rich discriminative features. Extensive experiments on four benchmark datasets with only 1% to 5% of the labeled samples per class show that Spiking-GSCViT matches or surpasses its ANN counterpart (94.16% on Indian pines and 97.71% on Salinas), with only 0.21 M parameters. The consecutive MAC operations are reduced by 81%, and the spike-driven synaptic operations (SOPs) are decreased by 39.2%. As a lightweight SNN-ViT hybrid architecture, Spiking-GSCViT simultaneously mitigates the data-hungry nature of both ViTs and SNNs, enabling accurate and energy-efficient HSIC under limited supervision.
author: Qiong Yao, Hao Liu, Yingxi Jin, Xiang Xu, Antonio Plaza

title: Few-Shot Open-Set Hyperspectral Pixelwise Classification With Spatial Aware Label Propagation
content: Pixelwise classification of hyperspectral images (HSI) is a fundamental task in remote sensing, but its deployment in real-world applications is often limited by the scarcity of labeled data and the presence of unknown classes at inference time. In this work, we propose Few-shot Open-set hyperspectral recognition from Self-Supervised Learning training (FOSSeL), a unified framework for few-shot, open-set hyperspectral pixelwise classification that does not require supervised training. The proposed approach first leverages self-supervised learning to construct a discriminative feature space from unlabeled data. Then, given a small set of labeled seed pixels, class predictions are obtained through spatially-aware graph-based label propagation over superpixel representations, enabling the joint exploitation of spectral similarity and spatial consistency. To address the open-set scenario, we introduce simple yet effective strategies to identify pixels that do not belong to the known classes. We evaluate FOSSeL on three benchmark hyperspectral datasets under multiple few-shot settings. The results show that the proposed framework achieves competitive or superior performance compared to fully supervised methods while maintaining robustness in the presence of unknown classes. These findings highlight the potential of combining self-supervised feature learning with graph-based inference for practical HSI analysis in low-annotation and open-world scenarios.
author: Matheus B. Pereira, Jefersson A. dos Santos, Laurent Najman

title: Cooperative Alignment and Boundary Refinement Network via Multisource Prior Synergy for Optical Remote Sensing Change Detection
content: Optical remote sensing change detection aims to identify changed pixels between bitemporal images of the same region, holding immense application value in fields such as urban planning and disaster assessment. However, disrupted by factors including seasonal transitions, illumination variations, and sensor viewpoint discrepancies, identical ground targets frequently exhibit pronounced spectral heterogeneity across bitemporal images. This heterogeneity hinders existing methods from effectively extracting robust change features, consequently leading to detection results frequently suffering from pseudochange responses and edge blurring. To address these challenges, we propose an RSCD architecture based on multisource prior synergy, named the Cooperative Alignment and Boundary Refinement Network, or CABRNet. Specifically, during the encoding phase, the Cooperative Spatiotemporal Alignment Module is embedded after each feature extraction layer. By aggregating cooperative representations of bitemporal features across both channel and spatial dimensions and modeling interchannel correlations, this module achieves dynamic feature alignment. Consequently, it extracts robust bitemporal features. During the feature fusion phase, the Confidence-Driven Boundary Modulator deeply integrates the physical high-frequency priors extracted via a Laplacian pyramid with the deep confidence priors generated through deep supervision. This integration collaboratively optimizes the edge representations of the fused features. During the decoding phase, the Signal-Preserving Context Aggregation Module is adopted to aggregate features. This strategy effectively mitigates the information loss induced by upsampling. Simultaneously, it enhances the reconstruction integrity of change regions and provides high-quality confidence priors for boundary modulation. Experimental results demonstrate that the CABRNet achieves F1 scores of 92.03%, 97.96%, and 83.92% on the LEVIR-CD, Lebedev, and SYSU-CD datasets, respectively. These results outperform existing state-of-the-art methods.
author: Canbin Hu, Sida Du, Xiaokun Sun, Fan Zhang

title: RSOFNet: PolSAR Target Recognition Using a Dual-Branch Framework Based on Rotational Similarity Features and Span-Conditioned Modulation
content: Restricted by view sensitivity and limited data volume, current polarimetric SAR vehicle target recognition still faces bottlenecks, including inadequate characterization of scattering properties and poor generalization performance. To address these limitations, this article proposes a rotation-domain similarity feature (RSF) to precisely characterize the angular dependence of target scattering characteristics and introduces an RSF-span overview-focusing network. The RSF matches the target coherency matrix with canonical scattering templates across the continuous rotation domain, yielding angle-dependent responses with explicit physical meaning. A span branch extracts sample-level scene context from the total-power image to guide RSF feature learning in a sample-adaptive top-down manner. A physics-constrained fusion layer integrates RSF-derived physical statistical priors, span-modulated mechanism-discriminative weights, and context-conditioned template reliability weights, ensuring physically interpretable feature embeddings. Experiments on the High-Resolution Airborne PolSAR Vehicle Target Recognition and GOTCHA datasets indicate that the proposed method achieves performance superior to data-driven, single-feature, and multifeature fusion baselines under standard, cross-depression-angle, and reduced-training-data conditions, with the advantage becoming more pronounced as sample size decreases.
author: Chanjuan Wang, Wei Wang, Jie Deng, Sinong Quan, Jun Zhang

title: Deep Clustering for Hyperspectral Images: A Comprehensive Survey From Single-View to Multiview Paradigms
content: Hyperspectral image (HSI) contains rich spectral information as well as spatial structural information, providing an important data source for a wide range of remote sensing applications. However, its high dimensionality, band redundancy, and the high cost of annotation limit the practical application of traditional methods that rely on supervised information. As a typical unsupervised learning task, clustering has received extensive attention. In recent years, with the rapid development of deep learning, deep clustering has significantly improved the unsupervised feature modeling capability for HSI by combining deep representation learning with clustering analysis. Moreover, it has gradually evolved from single-view modeling to multiview collaborative modeling, becoming an important research trend in this field. This article presents a systematic survey of deep clustering for HSI. It first introduces the basic concepts of HSI, deep clustering, and multiview clustering. Then, following the technical evolution from single-view to multiview paradigms, existing methods are systematically reviewed and categorized. Next, mainstream public datasets, commonly used evaluation metrics, and experimental comparisons of representative methods are summarized. Finally, this survey discusses the main challenges in current research, including cross-scene generalization, computational efficiency, multiview fusion effectiveness, robustness to uncertainty, as well as semantic interpretability, and further outlines potential directions for future research.
author: Jianing Wang, Lianmeng Jiao, Xinpeng Yang, Quan Pan

title: PVPSAM: Method and Benchmark for Weakly Supervised Object-Level Photovoltaic Panels Extraction in Remote Sensing Imagery
content: In recent years, the rapid and accurate extraction of photovoltaic (PV) footprints from remote sensing images (RSIs) has become a prominent research focus, particularly with deep learning (DL). However, as RSI resolution improves and the demand for finer extraction increases, current DL-based algorithms face substantial challenges. High-precision, fully supervised PV segmentation relies heavily on massive, high-quality object-level annotated data, which is highly time-consuming and labor-intensive to obtain. In contrast, contour-level annotations are simpler and more accessible, making them ideal for larger-scale model training. Therefore, we propose a novel two-stage weakly supervised PV segmentation framework, termed PV progressive SAM (PVPSAM), based on the segment anything model (SAM). In the first stage, we fine-tune an SAM-based contour decoder (C-Dec) using abundant contour-level annotated samples to learn the PV segmentation task. In the second stage, we use the segmentation outputs as dense prompts to iteratively fine-tune a refine decoder (R-Dec) with a small amount of object-level data, progressively achieving high-precision results. PVPSAM achieves state-of-the-art performance on our newly proposed multiscene dataset, GF-PVCOWS. Additionally, we verify its value for optimizing traditional datasets: through our developed PVRefineTool, original contour-level annotations can be converted into refined object-level data. Our work provides a new paradigm for large-scale RSI-based PV extraction.
author: Fangzhou Han, Xiaoci Li, Li Gu, Li Li, Ke Mi, Shengming Gu, Hailong Zhang

title: Integrated Multipattern Building Risk Assessment Based on MT-InSAR Measurements
content: Interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) has emerged as one of the most powerful remote sensing techniques for monitoring ground surface deformation, offering millimeter-level displacement measurements at large scale with high temporal frequency. In the context of urban infrastructure monitoring, InSAR measurements provide dense pointwise observations distributed across building facades and rooftops, capturing subtle yet critical deformation signals that precede structural deterioration or failure.However, most InSAR-based building assessment methods rely on a single indicator, which captures only limited aspects of structural deformation and may lead to incomplete risk assessments. To address this limitation, this study proposes a deformation pattern decomposition framework that constructs a dominant inclination plane for each building and decomposes the InSAR-derived deformation into three fundamental components grounded in geotechnical engineering knowledge, namely the uniform, tipping, and curvature components. Risk levels are evaluated for each component individually against established engineering thresholds and damage criteria, and subsequently integrated into a comprehensive staged assessment. The proposed method was successfully applied to the Tseung Kwan O industrial estate and Lohas Park, both newly reclaimed areas in Hong Kong. The results demonstrate its capability to effectively identify buildings at potential risk in proximity to ongoing construction projects, buildings influenced by large loads from tank farm facilities, and newly developed buildings undergoing postconstruction consolidation settlement. These findings confirm the effectiveness and practical applicability of the proposed methodology.
author: Yi Zheng, Sizhe Liu, Chang Yu, Fangxu Deng, Peifeng Ma

title: Deep Unfolding for Heterogeneous Change Detection: A Latent Calibration and Structured Separation Approach
content: Heterogeneous change detection (HCD) is essential for Earth's surface monitoring with multisource remote sensing data, especially in scenarios where strictly homogeneous bitemporal observations are unavailable. However, the significant modality gap caused by different imaging mechanisms makes direct comparison unreliable, as unchanged regions may still exhibit pronounced cross-modal discrepancy. Existing methods have made progress in feature alignment and representation learning, yet they still face two persistent difficulties: establishing statistically calibrated and comparable cross-modal representations, and isolating true change responses from modality-induced interference during change extraction. To address these limitations, this article proposes an iterative collaborative decomposition and fusion network (ICDF-Net), which formulates HCD as a latent representation decomposition problem and integrates latent calibration with structured decomposition through a unified end-to-end framework. Specifically, an adaptive heterogeneous collaborative module is designed to construct more stable cross-modal latent representations by performing collaborative feature calibration. Based on the calibrated latent representations, a deep unfolding low-rank and sparse decomposition module is introduced to promote the separation of low-rank background and sparse residual components. The sparse residual components are then combined with differences between the calibrated representations and reconstructed by a hierarchical sparse reconstruction decoder to obtain the final change map. Experimental results on three benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed ICDF-Net, which achieves the highest F1-scores with low model complexity and competitive inference efficiency.
author: Yankun Huang, Zhiguo Liang, Yun Zhang, Jiaojiao Tian, Zeyuan Li

title: FoilFormer: A Dual-Path Transformer-Based Network With Learnable Wavelet Transforms for ToA Estimation in eLoran Systems
content: One of the most critical challenges in enhanced long-range navigation (eLoran) systems is accurate time-of-arrival (ToA) estimation of sky and ground waves, commonly referred to as sky–ground wave recognition, which is essential for high-precision positioning. In this article, we propose the FoilFormer, a physics-guided dual-path Transformer architecture with the learnable wavelet transforms (WT) for ToA estimation. The proposed framework exploits eLoran signal characteristics for representation learning via three tightly coupled components: a learnable WT-based decomposition and feature fusion mechanism, a dual-path encoder, and a sparse attention module. First, motivated by the low-frequency and high-frequency structure of eLoran signals, we introduce the learnable discrete WT and inverse WT modules for adaptive multiscale decomposition and cross-scale feature fusion, enabling separation of components associated with different propagation behaviors. Second, we develop a dual-path encoder to process the decomposed components in parallel, preserving their distinct characteristics and improving the separation of overlapping arrivals. Third, we design a sparse attention mechanism tailored to eLoran signals to enhance salient time–frequency features while suppressing interference-induced redundancy. The experimental results show that the FoilFormer outperforms the representative inverse fast Fourier transform, the fourth-order cumulant multiple signal classification, the weighted Fourier transform and relaxation, the Levenberg–Marquardt, the deterministic maximum likelihood, the support vector machine, the extreme gradient boosting, and the artificial neural network, improving the ToA estimation success rates on the simulation data from $-10$ to 10 dB by 42.9%, 44.7%, 29.8%, 35.2%, 16.5%, 63.3%, 19.3% and 7.9%, respectively, and reducing the average distance deviation on the realistic data by 37.8%, 86.7%, 74.6%, 38.6%, 37.8%, 75.2%, 38.0%, and 34.9%, respectively.
author: Lianyu Li, Yuzhou Li, Kanghua Huang, Chunxiao Jiang, Zheng Dou

title: Multimodal Remote Sensing Image Matching Considering Structural Saliency
content: Nonlinear radiometric distortion, orientation reversal, and image rotation considerably affect multimodal image matching performance in remote sensing. Furthermore, existing multimodal image matching algorithms are highly complex and inefficient. We addressed these issues by developing a reliable matching method considering structural saliency (RMSS) for multimodal remote sensing images. First, we propose a method to describe structural saliency, which reliably represents both structural intensity and directional information. Second, we achieve rotation invariance in the descriptors by integrating structural information with a directional histogram descriptor framework. Subsequently, we design a coarse-to-fine matching strategy and propose an adaptive fast sample consensus improvement algorithm, which effectively enhances matching stability and accuracy. Finally, we design a two-stage subpixel refinement strategy to further improve localization accuracy and the number of matched points. The comparison of RMSS with seven state-of-the-art algorithms using six types of multimodal remote sensing images as experimental data demonstrates that the RMSS is simple to implement, exhibits high robustness to rotation in multimodal images, and can substantially improve the number and localization accuracy of matching points and the correct matching rate.
author: Li Xue, Yehua Sheng, Shuwen Yang, Xiangqiang Min, Xiu Lu

title: Flood Mapping Using Sentinel-1 Dual-Polarimetric SAR Data in Agricultural Landscapes
content: Monitoring flood-affected agricultural fields is important because flooding can significantly reduce crop productivity, threatening food security and livelihoods. Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data are well suited for flood monitoring because they are independent of weather conditions and can be acquired both day and night. Polarimetric SAR observations help distinguish different scattering mechanisms, aiding in the identification of flooded surfaces. Previous studies have mainly relied on fully polarimetric SAR data to analyze the impacts of floods on agricultural fields. Although dual-polarized Sentinel-1 SAR data are widely used for flood mapping, the use of descriptors derived from dual-polarized SAR data to identify flood-affected agricultural fields remains limited. To address this gap, this study introduces a Sentinel-1 agricultural flood descriptor (SAFD) for monitoring flood-affected agricultural fields using dual-polarized SAR data. The proposed method uses the dual-pol radar surface index to isolate surface-like scattering mechanisms. The methodology is tested using Sentinel-1 SAR data processed in Google Earth Engine over two flood-prone Indian states, Bihar and Odisha. Bihar experienced a major flood in 2019, while Odisha faced severe flooding in 2022 due to intense monsoon rainfall. The results show that SAFD effectively detects flood-affected agricultural fields across different regions. Validation with rain-gauge data confirms that high SAFD values are strongly linked to flood-inducing rainfall. Overall, the findings demonstrate that SAFD is a reliable and scalable approach for large-area agricultural flood monitoring using dual-polarized Sentinel-1 SAR data.
author: Shubhayan Roy Chowdhury, Dipankar Mandal, Abhinav Verma, Gerardo Di Martino, Avik Bhattacharya

title: A High-Accuracy GNSS Tropospheric Wet Delay Forecasting Algorithm via PINN-LSTM Integration Tailored to Complex Mountainous Terrain and Urban Environments: Methodology and Validation
content: The rapid expansion of low-altitude uncrewed aerial system (UAS) operations in complex mountainous urban environments have created urgent demand for high spatiotemporal resolution water vapor observations to support safe flight, precise navigation, and growth of the low-altitude economy. To address this unmet need, this study develops and validates a framework for the refined construction and forecasting of zenith wet delay (ZWD)—a core metric for precipitable water vapor estimation—across discrete atmospheric pressure levels, using Chongqing, China, a representative complex mountainous urban region, as a case study. We integrate in situ meteorological station observations with multilevel pressure ERA5 reanalysis data to retrieve ZWD values at the surface, 900 and 800 hPa levels using the Askne and Nordius model, followed by a comprehensive assessment of retrieval data reliability. We then develop a random forest interpolation algorithm to generate continuous, layered ZWD fields at 1 km spatial resolution across the study domain. Finally, we design a hybrid physics-informed neural network and long short-term memory (PINN-LSTM) model to produce high-accuracy ZWD forecasts for each target pressure level. Experimental results demonstrate three key findings: first, station-retrieved ZWD values show strong agreement with both Vienna Mapping Function (VMF) and radiosonde reference datasets, with correlation coefficients exceeding 0.95 for all validation comparisons and consistent variation trends, confirming the suitability of the retrieved data for multilevel ZWD forecasting research. Second, ZWD high-value and low-value zones exhibit distinct spatial distribution patterns across different seasons and pressure levels. Overall, ZWD decreases systematically as atmospheric pressure declines (i.e., at increasing altitude). Third, the PINN-LSTM model significantly outperformed both PINN and LSTM in predicting ZWD at different pressure levels across meteorological stations, demonstrating superior predictive accuracy, stability, and generalization capability. Compared with PINN and LSTM, PINN-LSTM reduced the average RMSE from 3.86 and 2.88 cm, respectively, to 1.51 cm, and decreased the average MAE from 2.83 cand 2.01 cm, respectively, to 1.01 cm. The layered ZWD construction and forecasting framework proposed in this study markedly improves the refined representation and predictive capability of low-altitude water vapor parameters in complex topographical regions. These findings provide critical support for meteorological assurance for UAS low-altitude flight, Global Navigation Satellite System navigation error correction, and the safe operation of the low-altitude economy.
author: Huan Zhang, Guihua Zhang, Bao Zhang, Mengzhu Peng, Zhizhong Wang, Jin Ma, Chaoqian Xu, Yibin Yao

title: Open-Vocabulary Forgetting in the Downstream Adaptation of Remote Sensing Vision–Language Detectors
content: Open-vocabulary detectors pretrained on remote sensing imagery can be queried with free-form category names instead of a fixed taxonomy. In practice, they reach applications through fine-tuning on small, specialized target datasets, and standard evaluation reports only target-dataset accuracy, so any loss of the pretrained open-vocabulary capability goes unmeasured. In this article, we present a retention-aware adaptation benchmark for remote sensing vision–language detectors: a fixed dual-axis protocol that evaluates every adapted model on target accuracy and on open-vocabulary retention, measured as mean average precision (mAP) on the 80-class LAE-80 C benchmark, with retention never used for model selection. Applying the protocol to LAE-DINO across one in-domain and three held-out targets shows that in-domain fine-tuning reduces retention from the pretrained 24.1 mAP by 0.8 mAP (3%), whereas held-out fine-tuning reduces it by 5.6 to 8.6 mAP (23% to 36%); under the fixed optimization budget of our experiments, the tested few-shot configurations lost more retention than full-data adaptation. Classwise and component-level diagnostics locate the loss on classes semantically close to the target vocabulary and show that it is not recoverable by restoring any single tested component, with prompt masking attributing about 12% of the distant-class loss to score competition. Across seven mitigation strategies, none produces a practically meaningful retention recovery at matched target accuracy or meets the predefined success criterion; weight interpolation of the final model dominates the early checkpoints, matches the later ones within the test-set uncertainty, and defines the best observed accuracy–retention frontier among the tested configurations. A second detector configuration, evaluated on its own natural-image vocabulary, reproduces the direction of these regularities. We release the protocol, splits, prediction files, and checkpoints as a reproducible benchmark.
author: Lefan Wang, Yuanrong He, Huilin Xu, Liang Zhong, Siyu Chen

title: A SARIMA-Kalman Graph-Transformer Framework for Spatiotemporal Prediction of SBAS-InSAR Acquired Surface Deformation in Tianjin Metropolitan Area
content: Severe surface deformation damages infrastructure and amplifies geohazard risk, calling for reliable long-horizon forecasts for early warning and loss mitigation. However, under low interferometric coherence and nonstationary noise, existing predictors rarely incorporate uncertainty information, underexploit local spatiotemporal structures, and may suffer from drift during recursive forecasting. We propose a seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average (SARIMA)-Kalman graph-transformer framework (SKGT) that forecasts grid-scale subsidence and generates spatially continuous deformation fields from Tianjin Sentinel-1A small baseline subset interferometric synthetic aperture radar (SBAS-InSAR) time series. Pixel-wise SARIMA-Kalman state-space modeling decomposes deformation into trend and residual components and estimates the trend states and their posterior covariance. The projected and standardized covariance is concatenated with the residual and state estimate as an auxiliary feature for residual prediction; it is not used as an explicit loss regularizer or attention-reweighting factor. The residual branch couples a spatial-neighborhood graph with a deformation-similarity graph, aggregates spatial features via SpatioGAT, and captures long-range dynamics using a sparse causal transformer with an autoregressive residual-increment update. The results show that SKGT achieves lower prediction errors than traditional statistical, learning-based, Transformer-based, and hybrid forecasting baselines, including GM, ARIMA, MLP, LSTM, PatchTST, and CEEMDAN-FTEA-GCN-Transformer, under the regional-scale testing protocol. In the three monitoring zones, SKGT obtains testing root mean square error values of 1.57 mm, 1.45 mm, and 1.42 mm, mean absolute error values of 1.25 mm, 1.16 mm, and 1.11 mm, and $R^{2}$ values of 0.74, 0.77, and 0.79, respectively. SKGT provides an interpretable and uncertainty-aware route to urban subsidence forecasting and risk assessment.
author: Yuheng Wu, Yifei Zheng, Cheng Zhang

title: A Physics-Based TOA Forward-Simulation Framework for Radiometric Stability Monitoring of Optical Satellites Over Forest Environments
content: Reliable radiometric monitoring of Earth observation satellites is often constrained by reliance on bright desert reference sites, which do not represent dark and heterogeneous vegetation targets. This study presents a physics-based top-of-atmosphere forward-simulation framework that integrates an automated forest ground radiometry network (KoFReN), directional reflectance homogenization using the RossThick–LiSparse–Reciprocal (RTLSR) model, and Py6S radiative transfer simulation constrained by collocated AERONET observations. Rather than providing a direct on-orbit validation of CAS500-4, this study evaluates the applicability of the framework through a Sentinel-2–based proxy assessment prior to CAS500-4 launch. The framework links hemispherical ground measurements to satellite-view geometry for radiometric evaluation over complex forest environments. Validation over five RadCalNet sites yielded gain ratios close to unity under homogeneous benchmark conditions, supporting the internal consistency of the forward-modeling chain. Application across eight Korean forest sites showed clear scene dependence, with terrain-driven representativeness and viewing geometry emerging as major limitations in heterogeneous landscapes, while geometry-aware screening improved NIR agreement under favorable conditions. A site-level representativeness analysis further showed that within-ROI reflectance heterogeneity, terrain variability, and illumination geometry help explain the magnitude of residual errors and their reduction after site-specific QC filtering. A data-driven uncertainty analysis indicated that internal processing-chain uncertainty is dominated by cosine-response correction and RTLSR-based BHR-to-BRF directional conversion. These results suggest the potential of distributed forest radiometry networks to support proxy-based prelaunch and early operational radiometric stability assessment over vegetation-dominated landscapes.
author: Joongbin Lim, Jeongho Lee, Wonkook Kim, Minji Seo, Cheonggil Jin, Byung-Oh Yoo

title: MSST-Net: Memory-Sustained Structure-Texture Representation Network for Remote Sensing Building Change Detection
content: Building change detection in remote sensing plays an important role in urban planning, land-use monitoring, and rapid postdisaster damage assessment. However, remote sensing images are inherently affected by illumination variations and seasonal changes, which introduce complex pseudochange noise. In addition, traditional hierarchical network architectures struggle to effectively balance multiscale structural boundaries and global texture consistency. To address these challenges, this article proposes a memory-sustained structure-texture representation network (MSST-Net). The network consists of three key components. Hierarchical group-grid coordination module is designed within the hierarchical backbone to suppress shallow feature noise, promote cross-scale collaboration among hierarchical features, and align spatial discrepancies. Bitemporal memory-augmented module is introduced, which integrates learnable memory matrices into the cross-attention mechanism to establish stable semantic correspondence between bi-temporal images. Structure-texture fusion module is further designed based on a structure–texture disentanglement strategy to separately refine the macroscopic structural information and fine-grained texture details of buildings, thereby accomplishing the change detection task. MSST-Net achieves F1 of 92.08%, 94.84%, and 89.39% on three public datasets LEVIR-CD, WHU-CD, and GZ-CD, respectively, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed network and the rationality of its architectural design.
author: Weibo Zhao, Qingqing Ming, Zhaolong Gao

title: Multistage Uncertainty-Aware Feature Fusion Framework for Semantic Segmentation of High-Resolution Remote Sensing Imagery
content: Semantic segmentation of high-resolution remote sensing imagery is essential for land-cover mapping, urban planning, and environmental monitoring. However, challenges such as spectral similarity, fine-grained boundaries, and class imbalance often produce ambiguous predictions in complex scenes. Conventional encoder–decoder architectures fuse multilevel features uniformly, ignoring prediction uncertainty and allowing unreliable features to propagate through the decoding hierarchy, causing boundary misalignment and semantic confusion. To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel uncertainty-aware decoding framework that integrates prediction uncertainty into a progressive coarse-to-fine refinement process. The framework introduces two complementary decoder-side modules. First, an Uncertainty-Gated Channel Module (UGCM) leverages uncertainty derived from intermediate decoder predictions to recalibrate encoder skip features at the channel level prior to fusion, suppressing ambiguous low-level responses while preserving informative structural details.
